targetTexts.1: A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
targetTexts.2: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
targetTexts.3: that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.
targetTexts.4: We will not hide them from their children but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might and the wonders He has performed.
targetTexts.5: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,
targetTexts.6: that the coming generation would know them—even children yet to be born—to arise and tell their own children
targetTexts.7: that they should put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments.
targetTexts.8: Then they will not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
targetTexts.9: The archers of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle.
targetTexts.10: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.
targetTexts.11: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.
targetTexts.12: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
targetTexts.13: He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.
targetTexts.14: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.
targetTexts.15: He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the seas.
targetTexts.16: He brought streams from the stone and made water flow down like rivers.
targetTexts.17: But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.
targetTexts.18: They willfully tested God by demanding the food they craved.
targetTexts.19: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
targetTexts.20: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”
targetTexts.21: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel,
targetTexts.22: because they did not believe God or rely on His salvation.
targetTexts.23: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.
targetTexts.24: He rained down manna for them to eat; He gave them grain from heaven.
targetTexts.25: Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.
targetTexts.26: He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.
targetTexts.27: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
targetTexts.28: He felled them in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
targetTexts.29: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.
targetTexts.30: Yet before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths,
targetTexts.31: God’s anger flared against them, and He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel.
targetTexts.32: In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; despite His wonderful works, they did not believe.
targetTexts.33: So He ended their days in futility, and their years in sudden terror.
targetTexts.34: When He slew them, they would seek Him; they repented and searched for God.
targetTexts.35: And they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
targetTexts.36: But they deceived Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues.
targetTexts.37: Their hearts were disloyal to Him, and they were unfaithful to His covenant.
targetTexts.38: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
targetTexts.39: He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return.
targetTexts.40: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
targetTexts.41: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
targetTexts.42: They did not remember His power—the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
targetTexts.43: when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
targetTexts.44: He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink.
targetTexts.45: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.
targetTexts.46: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.
targetTexts.47: He killed their vines with hailstones and their sycamore-figs with sleet.
targetTexts.48: He abandoned their cattle to the hail and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
targetTexts.49: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity—a band of destroying angels.
targetTexts.50: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
targetTexts.51: He struck all the firstborn of Egypt, the virility in the tents of Ham.
targetTexts.52: He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
targetTexts.53: He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.
targetTexts.54: He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired.
targetTexts.55: He drove out nations before them and apportioned their inheritance; He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
targetTexts.56: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
targetTexts.57: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.
targetTexts.58: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.
targetTexts.59: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.
targetTexts.60: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
targetTexts.61: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.
targetTexts.62: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.
targetTexts.63: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
targetTexts.64: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
targetTexts.65: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.
targetTexts.66: He beat back His foes; He put them to everlasting shame.
targetTexts.67: He rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim.
targetTexts.68: But He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.
targetTexts.69: He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever.
targetTexts.70: He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
targetTexts.71: from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance.
targetTexts.72: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
